newsitem.title: UK: Yemen-Eritrea dispute goes to arbitration.
newsitem.headline: Yemen-Eritrea dispute goes to arbitration.

text.p: An international arbitration court began meeting on Tuesday in London to resolve a dispute between Yemen and Eritrea over Red Sea islands lying on busy oil tanker routes, diplomatic sources said.
The five-judge panel's first meeting was a procedural session to discuss how the hearing would proceed.
"They would like to get to know each other and discuss procedure," one diplomatic source said. "Substantive issues will be tackled later."

Yemen has appointed an Egyptian and an American to the arbitration panel while Eritrea named an American and a Briton. Both countries have agreed on a fifth person, British judge Sir Robert Jennings, to head the panel.
Arab Yemen and African Eritrea signed an accord last October in Paris to set up the arbitration court in London.
Both countries claim sovereignty over the small, arid Hanish islands. The dispute led to clashes in which at least 12 people died in December 1995.
The court is expected to take several months to deliver two rulings, the first on the question of territorial sovereignty of the zone, and the second fixing maritime frontiers.
The islands are near shipping lanes used by more than 100 vessels daily on a route where tankers carry 125,000 barrels of oil a day from the Gulf to Europe via Egypt's Suez Canal.

The conflict worsened last August when Yemen threatened to take military action if mediation failed to defuse a crisis triggered by dispatch of Eritrean troops to Lesser Hanish island. Eritrea later said it had withdrawn its forces.
